The user wants to set up a second workspace for the repo at `/home/user/myproject-workspace2`. 

Looking at the CLAUDE.md file, I can see this project uses Jujutsu (`jj`) for version control, not git. The instructions say to use `jj` for all version control work.

For setting up a second workspace in jj, I should use `jj workspace add`. Looking at the available commands in the jj documentation provided, I can see there's a `jj-workspace-add` reference.

The general syntax for creating a new workspace would be:
```
jj workspace add [OPTIONS] <WORKSPACE_ROOT>
```

Where `<WORKSPACE_ROOT>` is the path where the new workspace should be created.

I should run `jj workspace add /home/user/myproject-workspace2` to create a new workspace at that location.

steps.message:
Done! I've created a second workspace for your jj repository at `/home/user/myproject-workspace2`. 

Both workspaces are now connected to the same repository and share the commit history, but each has its own independent working copy. You can switch between them using `jj workspace list` to see all available workspaces, or navigate to the new workspace directory directly.
steps.reasoning_content:
Perfect! The workspace was successfully created. I can see:
1. The original workspace "default" is at `.` (the current directory, `/home/user/myproject`)
2. The new workspace "myproject-workspace2" is at `../myproject-workspace2` (which is `/home/user/myproject-workspace2`)

Both workspaces are part of the same jj repository and can share the same commit graph while having independent working copies.
